title: The generic singleton of a fine ordinary monoid chart is affine
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space equipped with a sheaf of commutative monoids. Let $U$ be an open of $X$, let $P$ be a fine monoid in the sense of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], and suppose that the restricted sheafed space $X|_U$ is isomorphic to the ordinary (unsharpened) monoid spectrum of $P$, with its local-fraction sheaf. Let $\eta\in U$ specialize to every point of $U$. Then there are an open $W$ of $X$ and a fine monoid $Q$ such that $W=\{\eta\}$ and $X|_W$ is isomorphic, as a sheafed space of monoids, to the ordinary monoid spectrum of $Q$. No torsion-freeness or sharpness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.2--3.1.4 and 3.1.10(ii), printed pp.98--100; localization at the generic point of a single ordinary monoid chart.

proof.text: Transport eta into Spec P. Because eta generalizes every point, it generalizes the empty prime. Specialization is inclusion of prime carriers (test all the basic opens), so eta is itself the empty prime. This also follows by T0 separation and the fact that the empty prime generalizes every point.

Choose finite monoid generators e_i and take their product a, with the empty product equal to 1. The minimal-neighborhood formula at the empty prime identifies D(a) with the intersection of all D(p). A prime in it has empty carrier, so D(a) is the singleton of the empty prime. Its localization is localization at the entire monoid, namely P^gp. Each generator becomes a unit because its complementary product divided by a is an inverse.

Put Q=P^gp. The images of the chosen generators and their inverses generate Q as a monoid, and a group embeds in its own group completion, so Q is fine. Its spectrum is a singleton, since a proper monoid ideal contains no unit and every element of Q is a unit. Evaluate local-fraction sections at the unique point of D(a) to identify them with Q. The monoid sheafification unit is bijective on this singleton by the trivial-cover theorem, applied via the equivalence between commutative monoids and additive commutative monoids. The same computation identifies the ordinary spectrum sheaf of Q on its singleton with Q. On the empty open both sheaves are terminal. These isomorphisms commute with all restrictions and therefore give a sheafed-space isomorphism over the unique homeomorphism of the singletons. Transport it along the original affine chart and the composition isomorphism for open restrictions.

theorem monoid_generic_singleton_affine (X : SheafedSpace CommMonCat.{u})
    (U : Opens X) (P : CommMonCat.{u}) (hP : FineFan.IsFine P)
    (e : X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding ≅
      { carrier := TopCat.of (FineFan.MonoidPrime P)
        presheaf := (FineFan.spectrumSheaf P).obj
        IsSheaf := (FineFan.spectrumSheaf P).property })
    (η : X) (hη : η ∈ U) (hgen : ∀ x : X, x ∈ U → η ⤳ x) :
    ∃ (W : Opens X) (Q : CommMonCat.{u}), FineFan.IsFine Q ∧
      (W : Set X) = {η} ∧ Nonempty
        (X.restrict W.isOpenEmbedding ≅
          { carrier := TopCat.of (FineFan.MonoidPrime Q)
            presheaf := (FineFan.spectrumSheaf Q).obj
            IsSheaf := (FineFan.spectrumSheaf Q).property })
